candidates.source_name: Portál otevřených dat ČR / Národní katalog otevřených dat (NKOD) — data.gov.cz
candidates.why_relevant: National open data catalogue operated by Digitální a informační agentura (DIA). It is the master index of every dataset the Czech state publishes as open data, including public-procurement datasets (VVZ/ISVZ, Registr smluv, ÚOHS decisions, ARES). For an A2 tender scout it is the single entry point from which all other structured procurement datasets can be enumerated and their distribution URLs (CSV/XML/API) harvested via DCAT-AP metadata.
candidates.legal_status: open data, published under open licence per Czech open-data legislation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest the DCAT-AP catalogue (SPARQL endpoint / dataset API) filtering by theme GOVE and keywords 'veřejné zakázky', then follow distribution URLs; re-harvest monthly to detect new/retired datasets.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs seed query on data.gov.cz open procurement datasets
queries_used: data.gov.cz otevřená data veřejné zakázky dataset

candidates.source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek (VVZ) — NIPEZ publication subsystem
candidates.why_relevant: The statutory Czech bulletin where all above-threshold contract notices, award notices (oznámení o výsledku) and modifications must be published under Act 134/2016 Sb. This is the authoritative primary record of Czech bank/public-sector payments tenders and their awarded suppliers and values. Migrated to the NIPEZ platform; a central data hub (cdz.vvz.nipez.cz) distributes structured notice data.
candidates.legal_status: official public register; reuse of published notices permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled retrieval of structured notice exports (XML per Vyhláška 345/2023 Sb.) plus CPV-filtered form parsing; keep notice IDs (evidenční číslo zakázky) as join keys to ISVZ and TED.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on VVZ open data / XML export; snowballed from portal-vz.cz
queries_used: Věstník veřejných zakázek otevřená data export XML VVZ

candidates.source_name: ISVZ — Informační systém o veřejných zakázkách, OpenData section (MMR)
candidates.why_relevant: MMR's analytical layer over the VVZ. Publishes an explicit OpenData section with procurement records from the Bulletin and electronic marketplaces in XML, XLS and CSV, refreshed monthly (15th, for the prior month), plus statistical outputs and the contracting-authority-profile validator. This is the cleanest bulk route to reconstruct historic Czech award series without scraping notice pages.
candidates.legal_status: government open data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly pull of the OpenData XML/CSV bundles; build a local warehouse keyed on zadavatel IČO + CPV + evidenční číslo; diff month over month to detect new awards.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on ISVZ statistics/open data
queries_used: ISVZ statistiky veřejných zakázek portal-vz.cz otevřená data ročenka
candidates.observed_blocker: site served over plain HTTP in search results; legacy ASP.NET pages may be unstable

candidates.source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj (nen.nipez.cz), incl. profil zadavatele XML export
candidates.why_relevant: The state e-procurement system hosting many contracting authorities' profiles. Exposes machine-readable XML exports of contracts on a profile (e.g. /profil/profilMsp/XMLdataVZ with date-range parameters), which is exactly the structured feed needed to reconstruct award history and contract end dates for a given authority (state bodies, ČNB-adjacent institutions, state banks).
candidates.legal_status: statutory publication duty; open access to profile data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate profiles of banking/finance-sector authorities, then pull XMLdataVZ with rolling od/do date windows; parse per the ministry's XSD schema for contracting-authority profiles.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on NEN profil zadavatele XML export; snowballed from NIPEZ support docs
queries_used: NEN nen.nipez.cz otevřená data profil zadavatele XML export

candidates.source_name: Registr smluv (ISRS) open data dumps — data.smlouvy.gov.cz
candidates.why_relevant: Act 340/2015 Sb. forces publication of contracts above CZK 50k excl. VAT by a broad set of public bodies, including state banks and public institutions. Monthly XML dumps (dump_<YYYY>_<MM>.xml) with an XSD carry the actual signed contract metadata — counterparty, value, effective date and often contract duration. This is the single best structured route to incumbent identity and contract expiry dates, i.e. the true re-tender trigger for the A2 workstream.
candidates.legal_status: open data, BUT dataset contains personal data — recipient becomes a GDPR controller per the publisher's own notice
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch monthly dump_YYYY_MM.xml files and re-fetch historic months periodically (publisher states past dumps are regenerated when contracts change); filter counterparty IČO against a banking/payments supplier list; apply GDPR minimisation on ingest.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on registr smluv open data dumps; snowballed from data.gov.cz
queries_used: registr smluv otevřená data dump XML data.smlouvy.gov.cz banka smlouva
data.gov.cz otevřená data veřejné zakázky dataset

candidates.source_name: ISRS aplikační rozhraní (Registr smluv API)
candidates.why_relevant: Documented machine interface to the contract register for querying/publishing records — an incremental alternative to full monthly dumps for near-real-time detection of newly signed banking/payments contracts.
candidates.access_status: public documentation; some operations may require registration
candidates.legal_status: official system interface, terms per ISRS documentation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Read the interface description page first to confirm which read operations are open vs. registered; use read endpoints for delta polling, fall back to dumps for backfill.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from Registr smluv open data page
queries_used: registr smluv otevřená data dump XML data.smlouvy.gov.cz banka smlouva

candidates.source_name: TED Open Data Service / TED Search API (EU)
candidates.why_relevant: All Czech above-EU-threshold notices are mirrored in TED. The Search API is documented as requiring no authentication and supports expert queries plus bulk XML download; TED also offers daily/monthly XML packages and historic archives back to the 1990s. This is the most reliable machine route to a complete, comparable historic series of Czech banking/payments award notices, and lets CZ be benchmarked against CEE peers.
candidates.legal_status: EU open data, reuse permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Expert query on the Search API filtered by country=CZ plus CPV families for banking/payment/IT services (30/48/66/72 groups); paginate and store raw eForms/TED XML; supplement with monthly bulk packages for backfill.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en query on TED bulk/API access for Czech notices
queries_used: TED europa.eu open data bulk download API notices Czech tenders

candidates.source_name: EU Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS) / data.europa.eu curated TED CSV
candidates.why_relevant: PPDS aggregates TED plus a growing set of national procurement datasets with dashboards; data.europa.eu also hosts a curated TED CSV covering 2006-2023 with the core 'who bought what from whom, for how much' fields — an easy analytical backbone for long historic series. Czech national-level data did not appear among the nationally onboarded datasets in what I found, so CZ coverage here is via the TED layer.
candidates.legal_status: EU open data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the curated TED CSV for long-horizon 2006+ analysis; monitor PPDS dashboards and national onboarding list for future CZ national dataset availability.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en query on data.europa.eu Czech procurement datasets
queries_used: data.europa.eu Czech public procurement dataset historical award notices

candidates.source_name: Opentender.eu — Czech Republic portal (DIGIWHIST)
candidates.why_relevant: DIGIWHIST/Hertie School portal built with Czech partner Datlab; standardises Czech tender records into a common schema with integrity/corruption-risk indicators and offers a bulk 'all data' download page. Excellent for cross-country comparison and for pre-cleaned historic award series with buyer/supplier normalisation.
candidates.legal_status: research project open data; check per-download licence
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the /all bulk download for the CZ country package; treat as a derived/normalised layer and re-validate key facts against VVZ/TED before acting. Note data may be stale relative to the live bulletin — check the last update date.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en seed query on Opentender/Datlab/Digiwhist
queries_used: opentender.eu Czech Republic procurement data Digiwhist Datlab

candidates.source_name: Datlab s.r.o. — commercial tender database & Datlab Tenders API
candidates.why_relevant: Czech data company behind Opentender and vsechnyzakazky.cz; markets a cleaned supplier and tender-documentation database covering 50+ countries with supplier risk profiling. An API documentation space exists on Apiary (digiwhist.docs.apiary.io). The highest-quality commercial route to normalised CZ award history and supplier identity resolution, if budget allows.
candidates.access_status: commercial / partly gated — pricing not published in what I found
candidates.legal_status: commercial licence required for the paid product; API terms unknown
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Contact for a trial/licence and evaluate the Apiary-documented API for CZ coverage and supplier identifiers; do not scrape the commercial product.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en queries on Datlab API/pricing; snowballed from Digiwhist member page
queries_used: opentender.eu Czech Republic procurement data Digiwhist Datlab
Datlab tenderdata API tenders database access pricing "datlab"

candidates.source_name: VsechnyZakazky.cz — alternative Czech procurement portal (Datlab)
candidates.why_relevant: Aggregates Czech contracts subject to the procurement act (excluding small-scale ones) from many contracting-authority profiles into one searchable index — useful to discover which authority profile a given banking/payments contract lives on, and to snowball into profile URLs that are otherwise hard to enumerate.
candidates.legal_status: third-party aggregator; check ToS before bulk collection
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword/CPV browsing to build an actor map of contracting authorities and incumbent suppliers, then pivot to the underlying official profile/VVZ record for authoritative data.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from Datlab profile; cs aggregator query
queries_used: vsechnyzakazky.cz zindex.cz hlídač státu API veřejné zakázky data

candidates.source_name: Hlídač státu — public procurement, contracts and ÚOHS decision datasets + API
candidates.why_relevant: Czech civic-tech watchdog that ingests VVZ, Registr smluv, subsidies, political links and the full ÚOHS decision collection since 1999, and explicitly offers an API and open data for developers. It cross-links buyer IČO to contracts, tenders and disputes in one place — the fastest way to assemble an incumbent's full public-sector footprint including litigation history.
candidates.access_status: public; API typically requires a free registered token
candidates.legal_status: NGO-run open data; attribution and API terms apply
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register for an API token, query by supplier/buyer IČO to pull tenders + contracts + ÚOHS decisions; use as an enrichment layer over official VVZ/ISRS records rather than as the system of record.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on Czech procurement watchdog APIs
queries_used: vsechnyzakazky.cz zindex.cz hlídač státu API veřejné zakázky data
ÚOHS sbírka rozhodnutí databáze veřejné zakázky vyhledávání rozhodnutí
candidates.observed_blocker: API access is token-based per the site's developer section

candidates.source_name: ARES — Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů, open data + REST API
candidates.why_relevant: Ministry of Finance registry of all Czech economic subjects, exposing a public REST (and legacy XML) API plus full open-data dumps mandated by government decree. Essential for supplier verification in A2: resolve a supplier name in a tender award to a canonical IČO, legal form, address, registration date and source registers — the join key across VVZ, Registr smluv, TED and justice.cz.
candidates.legal_status: open data; MF reserves the right to throttle abusive use (documented threshold around 500 requests/minute)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the REST API for on-demand IČO lookups with polite rate limiting well under the stated cap; take the periodic open-data dump from data.mf.gov.cz / NKOD for bulk entity resolution instead of hammering the API.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs seed query on ARES/justice.cz supplier verification
queries_used: ARES ekonomické subjekty API otevřená data obchodní rejstřík justice.cz
candidates.observed_blocker: publisher documents throttling of heavy users (~500 req/min)

candidates.source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz) — Ministry of Justice
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative commercial register plus the Collection of Deeds (sbírka listin) holding filed annual reports, financial statements, founding documents and statutory-body changes for every Czech legal entity. For A2 this converts a winning supplier into a verifiable financial and ownership profile — revenue scale, auditor, group structure — and reveals ownership changes that reshape incumbency.
candidates.legal_status: public register; documents are PDFs, many scanned
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Look up by IČO obtained from ARES, then enumerate sbírka listin entries and download annual reports (účetní závěrka / výroční zpráva) as PDFs for the incumbent set; OCR scanned filings.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on sbírka listin and open data of public registers
queries_used: or.justice.cz sbírka listin výroční zpráva API veřejný rejstřík data

candidates.source_name: dataor.justice.cz — OpenData ISVR (public registers bulk open data)
candidates.why_relevant: The bulk open-data distribution of the Czech public registers (ISVR), with exports in CSV/XML. Lets a scout build a local mirror of legal-entity master data — including historic states of directors, addresses and legal form — instead of scraping or.justice.cz page by page, which is the sustainable way to run supplier verification at scale.
candidates.legal_status: open data of the Ministry of Justice
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic bulk download of the XML/CSV register exports; maintain a slowly-changing-dimension table of legal entities so historic tender awards resolve to the entity state at award time.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from or.justice.cz search results
queries_used: or.justice.cz sbírka listin výroční zpráva API veřejný rejstřík data

candidates.source_name: Sbírka rozhodnutí ÚOHS — decisions dataset on NKOD / uohs.gov.cz
candidates.why_relevant: The competition authority's decision collection since 1999, also published as an open dataset in NKOD and mirrored by Hlídač státu. Challenged tenders are a strong signal: they reveal disputed award criteria, aggressive incumbents and, critically, tenders whose timeline slipped — which changes the re-tender window a scout would otherwise infer from contract expiry alone.
candidates.legal_status: official register / open dataset in NKOD
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Ingest the NKOD dataset distribution rather than scraping; filter decisions by buyer IČO and by keywords for payments/IT subject matter.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on ÚOHS decision database; confirmed NKOD dataset entry
queries_used: ÚOHS sbírka rozhodnutí databáze veřejné zakázky vyhledávání rozhodnutí

candidates.source_name: E-ZAK ČNB — Czech National Bank contracting-authority profile
candidates.why_relevant: The single most sector-relevant contracting-authority profile for CZ banking: ČNB (IČO 48136450, VVZ profile ID 342165) publishes its tenders and, below thresholds (CZK 3m supplies/services), contracts that never reach the VVZ. Unregistered users get basic contract info and tender documentation. Its archive is where historic ČNB payments/IT awards and their durations can be reconstructed.
candidates.access_status: public for basic data; some documents may require registration
candidates.legal_status: statutory profil zadavatele publication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the profile listing and the E-ZAK XML profile export if offered; also cross-check the gemin.cz mirror referenced by ČNB and the ČNB povinné odkazy page for profile relocations.

candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — CDX Server API
candidates.why_relevant: Czech tender portals routinely purge or relocate expired notices (VVZ migrated to NIPEZ; old.vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz artefacts still circulate). The CDX Server API allows querying every archived capture of a URL or URL prefix with date, MIME and status-code filters, so a scout can recover the text of award notices, profile listings and supplier pages that no longer exist live — the only practical route to pre-migration Czech notice history.
candidates.legal_status: Internet Archive terms; archived third-party content retains its own rights
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query the CDX endpoint with matchType=prefix on domains such as vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz, vvz.nipez.cz, ezak.cnb.cz and supplier sites, filter statuscode:200 and CZ-relevant paths, then fetch the specific timestamped snapshots; rate-limit and cache locally.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en seed query on Wayback CDX for expired notices
queries_used: Wayback Machine CDX API archive.org snapshots expired tender notice
candidates.observed_blocker: CDX endpoint is known to throttle heavy prefix queries

candidates.why_relevant: Academic scoring methodology for Czech contracting authorities built on VVZ data, contracting-authority profiles and other tender sources over rolling three-year windows. Its wiki pages document exactly which data fields exist, where they are unreliable, and how supplier dependence (share of public contracts in total revenue) can be computed — a free methodological map of the CZ procurement data landscape and its quality traps.
candidates.legal_status: academic/NGO publication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Read once to calibrate field-level trust in VVZ/profile data; re-check periodically for methodology updates rather than scraping.

negative_findings.description: Searched for Czech national procurement datasets onboarded into the EU Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS). Results listed TED (2021+) and national datasets for Austria, Germany, Finland and Norway, but no Czech national dataset appeared among them.
negative_findings.result_summary: CZ coverage in PPDS appears to be only via the EU-wide TED layer, i.e. above-threshold notices only; below-threshold Czech contracts are not reachable there.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A scout relying on PPDS alone would systematically miss the below-EU-threshold banking/payments contracts, which in CZ are precisely where many card, terminal and paper-consumables purchases sit. National routes (ISVZ OpenData, NEN profile XML, Registr smluv) remain mandatory.

negative_findings.description: Searched in English for Datlab's tender database API access and pricing. Found the company site, the Digiwhist member page and an Apiary documentation space (digiwhist.docs.apiary.io), but no published pricing, licence terms or self-service API key flow.
negative_findings.result_summary: Datlab commercial access conditions are opaque from open sources; a direct commercial enquiry is required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Datlab is the highest-quality normalised CZ tender/supplier source. Not knowing cost or licence terms blocks a build-vs-buy decision for the A2 collection stack and risks planning around data that may be unaffordable or contractually unusable.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching for procurement open data combined with banking terms did not surface any dataset scoped to the banking or payments sector; all CZ procurement datasets found are horizontal (all sectors), sliceable only by CPV code or buyer IČO.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ready-made banking/payments procurement dataset exists for CZ; sector scoping must be constructed by the collector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collection design must own CPV-code and buyer-list curation (e.g. CPV 30/48/66/72 families plus a hand-built list of banks, ČNB, state financial institutions). Without that, sector recall will be driven by keyword luck rather than a defined frame.

negative_findings.description: References to old.vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz appeared only indirectly, via a municipal site's file-download link, while current VVZ content sits under the NIPEZ domains (vvz.nipez.cz, cdz.vvz.nipez.cz). I did not fetch the legacy domain and cannot state whether it resolves.
negative_findings.result_summary: The pre-NIPEZ VVZ domain appears superseded; status unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historic Czech notice URLs captured in older research or link collections are likely to be dead or redirected, so historic reconstruction should route through Wayback CDX prefix queries on the legacy domain rather than assuming live retrieval.

negative_findings.description: There is no established Czech-language term for web-archive infrastructure equivalent to 'CDX API'; searching for archive-based recovery of expired Czech notices had to be conducted in English against Internet Archive documentation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Archive-tooling discovery was English-only by necessity; the Czech national web archive (Webarchiv, NK ČR) was not investigated in this slice.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Webarchiv.cz may hold Czech-domain captures the Internet Archive lacks, particularly for government sites under legal-deposit crawling, so an archive route may be under-covered.

coverage_gaps.description: The Czech national web archive (Webarchiv, operated by the National Library of the Czech Republic) was not searched or assessed in this slice, despite being the most likely holder of deep historic captures of .cz government and supplier sites.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated cs pass on 'Webarchiv Národní knihovny ČR', 'webarchiv.cz sklizeň', 'archivace webu veřejná správa' and assess its search/API access and whether captures are publicly retrievable or reading-room-only.

coverage_gaps.description: For several key structured routes — VVZ/cdz.vvz.nipez.cz distribution, the NIPEZ Registr veřejných zakázek consumer interface, and the ISVZ OpenData download paths — I identified the systems but did not establish exact endpoint URLs, schema versions or authentication requirements.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch portal-vz.cz's profil zadavatele XML/XSD documentation and the NIPEZ service-usage rules, then record concrete endpoint URLs, schema versions (incl. Vyhláška 345/2023 Sb. forms) and any registration requirement in the source register.

coverage_gaps.description: The contracting-authority side is mapped only for ČNB. The wider CZ banking/payments buyer set — commercial banks that are not public contracting authorities, Národní rozvojová banka, Česká pošta, state institutions with card/terminal estates — has not been resolved to profile URLs or IČOs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an IČO-keyed buyer list via ARES, then resolve each to its profil zadavatele (NEN or commercial platform) and record the per-buyer structured collection route; note explicitly which buyers are outside the procurement act and therefore invisible in these datasets.

coverage_gaps.description: No source found in this slice directly exposes contract END dates as a queryable field; expiry must be derived from Registr smluv contract metadata (effective date plus stated duration) or from framework-agreement terms in tender documentation.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Prototype an expiry-derivation rule over Registr smluv XML for a sample of financial-sector buyers and measure what share of contracts yield a usable end date; document the residual blind spot.

coverage_gaps.description: The Registr smluv publisher explicitly warns that its dataset contains personal data and that the recipient becomes a GDPR controller. No handling policy has been defined for this slice's recommended bulk ingestion.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a minimisation and retention policy before ingesting ISRS dumps: drop natural-person counterparties and signatory names at parse time, retain only legal-entity records, and document the lawful basis for the remainder.

coverage_gaps.description: Certified Czech e-procurement platforms other than NEN — Tender arena, E-ZAK instances beyond ČNB, Gemin, e-zakazky.cz, vhodne-uverejneni.cz — were identified only in passing; their statutory XML profile-export endpoints were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each certified electronic tool, locate its standard profile XML export URL pattern and record one worked example, so that any buyer can be collected structurally once its platform is known.

brief: The Czech open-data layer for procurement is unusually rich and almost entirely machine-readable: data.gov.cz (NKOD) indexes everything, VVZ/NIPEZ plus MMR's ISVZ OpenData carry the statutory notice and award record in XML/CSV, NEN exposes per-authority profile XML exports, and TED mirrors all above-threshold CZ notices through an unauthenticated Search API. The decisive asset for the A2 workstream is the Registr smluv (ISRS) bulk XML dump, which uniquely carries signed-contract metadata — counterparty, value and effective date — and is therefore the only realistic route to incumbent identity and contract-expiry timing, at the cost of an explicit GDPR-controller obligation the publisher places on every recipient. Supplier verification is well served by ARES (open REST API plus bulk dumps) joined to or.justice.cz / dataor.justice.cz for filed annual reports and ownership, with Hlídač státu, Opentender/Datlab and zIndex acting as normalised or methodological overlays rather than systems of record. Two structural weaknesses remain: no CZ dataset is scoped to banking or payments, so sector framing must be built from CPV codes and a curated buyer list; and expired or pre-migration notices are recoverable only through Wayback CDX prefix queries, with the Czech national Webarchiv still unassessed.
